extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor, mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis. The rig captured equirectangular images at 30 fps and LiDAR data at 10 fps. Data were collected across 29 video sequences in indoor and outdoor settings on a university campus under various weather and lighting conditions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing data due to sparse LiDAR point clouds were addressed via depth completion, which increased label density from 12% to 61%.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of equirectangular images from two Ricoh Theta V cameras and point clouds from an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Depth completion pipeline: temporal aggregation of point clouds from 4 preceding and 4 succeeding frames, interpolation using weighted average of k-nearest neighbors (k=17) in spherical coordinates, filtering based on uncertainty (relative weighted variance) and out-of-distribution threshold (average distance to neighbors).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were cropped to remove unnecessary borders (sky, ground) and downsized from 3840x1920 to 1920x512 pixels. LiDAR point clouds were projected onto equirectangular images using optimized rotation and translation parameters. Depth completion was applied to increase label density.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Depth and disparity labels were obtained by projecting LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images. The projection was optimized by minimizing the error between projected points and manually selected corresponding image points. Depth completion was applied to augment labels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment accuracy was assessed by calculating pixel error between projected LiDAR points and image positions, resulting in an average error of 1.7 pixels (8.0 pixels for challenging areas).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LiDAR-to-image mapping optimization using BFGS algorithm; depth completion using k-nearest neighbors interpolation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Depth completion may introduce errors at object boundaries; temporal aggregation limited for fast-moving objects; dataset collected on a university campus, may not generalize to all environments.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, and validation of omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models; benchmarking stereo matching methods; cross-scene generalization analysis.
